newsitem.title: USA: IDEX sees record results in 1997.
newsitem.headline: IDEX sees record results in 1997.

text.p: IDEX Corp said Tuesday that it expects to set records in sales, net income and earnings per share in 1997.
The company said it based this projection, barring unforeseen circumstances, in part on an outlook for modest economic growth in both the United States and world markets.

Other factors that will help 1997 results include a focus on further international growth, inclusion of Fluid Management, which was acquired in July 1996, for a full year, use of strong cash flow to cut debt and interest expense, and opportunities to further improve operating margins in newly acquired businesses, the company said.

Earlier, IDEX, which makes proprietary fluid handling and industrial products, announced fourth quarter earnings of $0.45 a share, up from $0.39 a year ago. For the year, earnings were a record $1.69 a share, up from $1.53.
Donald Boyce, chairman, said the company has achieved a 22 percent compound average rate of growth in earnings since it was formed in 1988.
Sales were a record $562.6 million in 1996, up from $487.3 million a year ago.

In 1996, IDEX said, acquisitions contributed significantly to sales and earnings improvement. Base business sales rose by only one percent, with moderate growth in most of its pump businesses being largely offset by declines in activity in capital goods related businesses.
International sales accounted for 41 percent of total revenues in 1996, up from 35 percent in 1995.
